p.SCOPE: This protocol governs long-running, multi-step development campaigns executed by humans and interchangeable central agents across sessions, branches and contributors. It defines where personal execution state lives, how a complete plan stays complete while its visible frontier changes, who may accept work, how ordinary continuation recovers from durable context, and how an explicitly requested formal central handoff moves without laundering unreviewed work into accepted state.

p.FRAMEWORK-NOT-AGENT: It is a framework for coordination. It does not implement a coding agent, choose an LLM provider, force an autonomous loop, or make LLM access mandatory. Any agent or human may drive it.

facts.PLANE-PROJECT: **Project authority** lives in owner instructions and repository evidence: specifications, tests, code, accepted decisions and maintainer/integrator policy. It is shareable across contributors and machines.
facts.PLANE-CONTRIBUTOR: **Contributor execution state** lives under that developer's `~/.vibe/steward/`: personal settings, branch/worktree context and adaptive plan. Custody is advisory coordination; formal handoff bundles exist only when the owner explicitly requests a transfer between central sessions on the same machine.
facts.PLANE-WORKER: **Worker state** lives in the worker's explicit task packet, ordinary worktree diff and report. A worker cannot promote itself to central, accept itself or mutate the central plan by implication.

p.AUTHORITY-ORDER: Where layers disagree: `Human > normative specification = executable specification > accepted code > shared project projection > user-local plan > handoff narrative > worker report`. Recency alone grants no authority.

facts.LAW-LOCAL-EXECUTION-STATE: **Personal execution state is local.** One developer's cursor, interaction preference, planning profile and central-session continuity never become a shared mutable repository file by default.
facts.LAW-SHARED-FACTS-IN-REPO: **Shared facts stay in the repository.** Product intent, stable decisions, tests, code, deliberately shared campaign contracts and accepted evidence cannot be hidden in a local plan or a model's memory.
facts.LAW-LOSSLESS-PLAN: **The plan is lossless, not merely current.** Every mandate item has a stable identity and remains owned by a node or carries an explicit disposition. Replanning changes the route; it never silently erases the obligation.
facts.LAW-ONE-CENTRAL-HOLDER: Retired v0.2 mandatory-holder law. Its current heirs are `LAW-CASUAL-CONTINUATION` and `LAW-SINGLE-LIVE-WRITER`.
facts.LAW-CASUAL-CONTINUATION: **Ordinary continuation needs no custody ritual.** After timeout, crash, compaction, new chat, model or provider-account change, quota exhaustion or provider overload, any owner-facing central agent may read the exact binding, settings, complete plan and tree and continue under the current owner instruction without session, handoff, receipt or takeover documents. Custody metadata does not grant or deny that authority.
facts.LAW-SINGLE-LIVE-WRITER: **One observed live central writer at a time.** Parallel workers may execute disjoint atoms, but an empirically observed conflicting central writer stops affected writes until the owner resolves it. Changed inputs invalidate the affected snapshot: attribute and recapture expected own writes or reconcilable external changes; escalate unresolved semantic or writer conflicts. Stale holder, session or heartbeat metadata alone is not a conflict verdict.
facts.LAW-CUSTODY-NOT-ACCEPTANCE: **Custody metadata does not transfer acceptance.** In ordinary continuation or explicit formal handoff, the next coordinator inherits artifacts and claims as evidence, never a predecessor's unrepeatable confidence. Durable project-accepted evidence remains history; dirty, worker and incomplete work remains candidate.
facts.LAW-UNIQUE-RECORDS: **Concurrent writers create uniquely named records; shared views are derived or integrator-owned.** A handwritten global counter, status line or `CONTINUE.md` is a conflict magnet, not collaboration infrastructure.
facts.LAW-SAME-QUALITY-FLOOR: **Profiles change scaffolding, never the quality floor.** `ultra` may use larger reasoning spans; `standard` compensates with smaller atoms and more checkpoints. Neither may omit scope, evidence, review or closure proof.
facts.LAW-HANDOFF-IS-TWO-PHASE: **An explicit formal handoff is offer plus receipt.** Writing a summary does not transfer the baton. Only an owner-requested formal handoff invokes this protocol: the outgoing session becomes write-fenced after sealing an offer, and the incoming session verifies and receipts it before the formal transfer advances.
facts.LAW-GOAL-IS-A-PROJECTION: **A campaign goal is a deterministic projection, never a second plan.** It selects one stable campaign node and renders its mandates, accepted boundary, candidates, remaining route and exit proof. `plan.toml` always wins on divergence.
facts.LAW-EXECUTION-SCOPE: **Current owner intent governs execution.** A stored goal, ready frontier or recovery checkpoint does not start a campaign when the owner requested planning, inspection or a stop. Existing authorization survives ordinary interruption within its scope; continuation does not require repeating already resolved approvals.
facts.LAW-RECOVER-EVIDENCE: **Recover evidence before repeating work.** Provider failure does not prove a failed operation. Inspect surviving artifacts, live jobs and remote effects before retrying; accepted unchanged evidence stays accepted, while unfinished decisions remain candidates. Recover concise recorded rationale, never claim to reconstruct lost internal reasoning. Retry bounds survive session and account changes.

td.ROLE-OWNER-AUTHORITY: Mandate, product and policy rulings; may assign or revoke other roles.

td.ROLE-OWNER-NOT: No automatic proof that an implementation works.

td.ROLE-MAINTAINER-AUTHORITY: Repository integration policy, merge/release authority granted by the project.

td.ROLE-MAINTAINER-NOT: Ownership of every contributor's local plan.

td.ROLE-INTEGRATOR-AUTHORITY: Shared campaign contract, integration queue and project-acceptance verdict within the granted campaign.

td.ROLE-INTEGRATOR-NOT: Permission to rewrite contributor history or erase contrary evidence.

td.ROLE-CENTRAL-AUTHORITY: Under current owner/project authority: this developer context's adaptive plan, workers, local gates, commits and explicitly requested formal handoff.

td.ROLE-CENTRAL-NOT: Authority from custody metadata, other contributors' branches or project-wide acceptance unless separately integrator.

td.ROLE-WORKER-AUTHORITY: Only the explicit packet and its file perimeter; reports evidence.

td.ROLE-WORKER-NOT: Central custody, acceptance, commits or status promotion.

p.ROLES-COME-FROM-PROJECT: A local file may record a role claim for coordination, but cannot grant the role. Actual authority comes from the owner and project policy. In a one-person project, one human may hold every role; the distinctions still protect handoffs and evidence.

p.MEMORY-CLASSIFY: A central coordinator classifies every durable discovery before accepting an atom: normative product law → specification; executable law → test; implementation fact → code or documentation; future work → issue/backlog record; project operating fact → repository policy; machine or personal preference → `~/.vibe/steward/`. Worker reports and local handoffs are evidence and archaeology, never the sole home of an accepted project fact.

p.NO-EARLY-CLEANUP: Do not delete a worker report, cache artifact, branch or worktree that may contain unique work or unpromoted knowledge. First inventory it, promote accepted facts, prove the product diff is integrated or intentionally rejected, then clean it.

facts.DOC-VERIFICATION: Selecting affected build/test targets, evidence reuse and partial-panel recovery: [`verification-selection.xml`](verification-selection.xml). Read when binding an execution packet or choosing checks; a milestone alone never selects the full product panel.
facts.DOC-RECOVERY: Quota, overload and interrupted operation recovery: [`interruption-recovery.xml`](interruption-recovery.xml). Read when dispatch may outlive the coordinator or an interruption occurs.

facts.NO-DISTRIBUTED-LOCK: No distributed lock or cross-machine consensus. Cross-machine transfer requires an explicit exported bundle and is deferred until a transport and identity model are specified.
facts.NO-ENFORCEMENT-CLAIM: No enforcement claim. Advisory custody, coherent snapshots and atomic replacement make conflicts reviewable; they cannot prevent a malicious or broken process from editing files or guarantee a cross-harness runtime lock.
facts.NO-PRODUCT-COMMAND: No `vibe.exe` command. Product users do not inherit campaign-maintainer controls merely because their project uses VibeVM.
facts.NO-MODEL-PROFILE: No model-name-specific profile in v0.1. Capability profiles remain stable when vendors rename, improve or regress models; model overlays may be added later.
